newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty still just below resistance, depos flat.
newsitem.headline: Zloty still just below resistance, depos flat.

text.p: The Polish zloty held virtually still in morning Thursday trade, perched a fraction below key resistance at 1.5 percent from the parity rate and dealers saw little movement for the rest of the day.
They said foreign investor entry into Polish fixed bonds on Wednesday, estimated by dealers at up to 200 million zlotys, had not yet gone through the market.

"The market is holding flat just below resistance with no (foreign investor) fixed bond entry seen, so the outlook is stable for today and the next few days," said Jaroslaw Dryjski, forex dealer at Bank Slaski SA.
The value date for the fixed bond tender is June 12.
At 0930 GMT the zloty was at 1.49/1.46 percent from parity, against opening's 1.50/1.45 percnet and Wednesday's close at 1.52/1.48 percent.
It was at 3.2255/59 to the dollar, against an opening rate of 3.2255/65 and at 1.8693/03 to the mark, against 1.8690/05.
Dealers said that foreign investors returned to buying Polish debt this week after withdrawaling some $400 million at the end of May following a collapse of the Czech crown.
"Investors are not buying large sums, but rather slowly building posistions," said Piotr Korcz of Bank Handlowy SA.

Dealers said some foreigners were still apprehensive about buying Polish paper because the economic situation in the Czech Republic may worsen further and possibly again weaken the zloty, along with other currencies of emerging markets.
On the money market one-day rates held flat as the market was fully liquid despite larger obligatory reserve outflows in June as banks had surplusses on average reserve positions.
Overnight were at 22.05/22.30 percent and tomorrow/next at 22.08/22.30 percent against opening's 22.00/22.30 and 22.10/22.25 percent respectively.
